P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Real-time location updates to many contacts (fan-out problem). Location precision reduction latency (should be fast). Audit logging at scale (every location access). Emergency override coordination (broadcast to affected users).
P.P2_defensibility: Granularity-based sharing prevents pinpoint tracking. Per-contact overrides enable fine-grained control. Audit trail enables privacy transparency. Emergency override documented and audited. Default to least precise (city) for safety.
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence in granularity logic (deterministic). High confidence in audit logging (straightforward). Medium confidence on emergency override (requires legal review and careful testing).
P4_failure_modes: Location granularity not applied → exact location exposed (mitigate: default to most restricted if error)
Audit log too slow → real-time location sharing blocked (mitigate: async audit logging, never block location sharing for audit)
Emergency override not revoked → location remains exposed after emergency (mitigate: auto-revert on event end, user manual revoke)
Contact override forgotten → user thinks location private but it's shared (mitigate: clear UI indication of current granularity)
P.P5_backup_plan: If granularity reduction fails: default to most restricted (city). If audit fails: log async, never block sharing. If emergency override fails: user can manually revert. If per-contact setting lost: fall back to default.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate granularity reduction failure. Test audit logging under high throughput (1M location events/min). Test emergency override activation/deactivation. Test edge cases: location at boundary of granularity levels.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for granularity reduction algorithm (test coordinates at boundaries). Integration tests for per-contact overrides. Load tests for location broadcasting (10k users, each sharing with 100 contacts). End-to-end tests for full location workflow. Audit trail validation (spot-check random samples). Emergency override testing (simulate event, verify override, verify revert).
P.P8_benchmarks: Granularity reduction: <50ms. Location broadcast: <2s for 100 recipients. Audit logging: <500ms (async). Emergency override: <5s activation. Per-contact override update: <1s. False positive (unintended sharing): 0%. Audit coverage: 100%.

CH1_change_log.description: Initial CONFolder for location sharing module

L.L1_legal_considerations: Location is highly sensitive PII. GDPR requires explicit consent per-use-case and granular controls. CCPA grants right to opt-out. Emergency override may be required by FEMA/ICS during declared emergencies, but requires legal authority documentation. Audit trail required for transparency.
L.L3_consent_requirements: Separate consent for: (1) location sensor access (GPS), (2) location sharing with contacts, (3) location history retention, (4) emergency location sharing (during declared emergency), (5) EMS access to location. All opt-in (no defaults). Granularity levels presented clearly (not abstract).
L.L4_liability_notes: Granularity labeling must be accurate (if 'neighborhood' actually means 5-block radius, say so). Emergency override requires clear legal authority and documentation. Audit trail enables privacy compliance verification. User confusion about granularity could lead to unintended exposure (legal risk). Mitigation: clear, plain-language descriptions of each level.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Location event storage: ~200B per event. At 10k users with 10 events/day, ~20MB/day = ~7GB/year storage. Audit log storage: ~500B per access. At 100k accesses/day, ~50MB/day = ~18GB/year. Total: ~25GB/year at 10k users.
F.F2_accounting_considerations: Storage cost scales with user base and event frequency. Tiered retention (delete old events after 90 days) can reduce costs. Consider data compression for archived events.
F.F3_revenue_impact: Location sharing enables group features and help matching (retention). Emergency response capability is competitive advantage. Positive impact.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Location encrypted at rest (AES-256). Granularity reduction happens server-side (server never exposes high-precision location to unintended users). Emergency override requires authentication and audit trail. Rate limiting on location queries (prevent scanning).
S.S2_data_privacy: Location data deletion: user can delete own location history. Granularity-based sharing prevents tracking. Audit log shows all accesses (transparency). Emergency override audited (accountability). Default to most restricted granularity if ambiguous.
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Location encrypted at rest (AES-256). Transiting TLS. Location history encrypted (per-user encryption key).
S.S4_access_control: Users see only location at their allowed granularity level. EMS access only during declared emergency (with audit trail). Admin cannot bypass granularity rules. Historical location access requires additional audit.
S.S5_audit_requirements: Comprehensive audit log: every location access (who accessed, when, at what granularity, context). Emergency override activation/deactivation. Location consent changes. Audit trail retention: 7 years (legal requirement).

X.X1_notes: Location sharing is core to Beacon's value prop (help matching, group formation, emergency response). Granularity levels are privacy-safety tradeoff: finer granularity helps response, coarser granularity protects privacy. Audit trail enables both privacy compliance and emergency response accountability.
X2_open_questions: Emergency override scope? (all data to EMS? only location? only in event zone?)
Retention policy? (rolling 24h, rolling 7 days, keep until deleted?)
Retroactive access revocation? (user can see who accessed, but can't unsee - acceptable?)
X.X3_related_research: GDPR location data requirements. FEMA emergency protocols. Differential privacy for location. Geohashing. Location granularity-to-distance mapping. Privacy-preserving maps.
